description.narrative:
Education sector is wide and challenges are so many. TEN/MET is aware of the challenges including the poor learning outcomes as reflected by poor pass rates in the national examinations at basic education level (primary and lower secondary education), poor literacy and numeracy skills of children, poor livelihood and poor implementation of education policies at all levels. TEN/MET as a coordination agency for CSOs education sector in Tanzania is only going to focus on few key activities that would impact in improving quality and equality of education sector in Tanzania.
1. Coordinating education sector by assessing and ultimately bring togather all actors in education to share challenges and success to better inform policy initiatives at higher level. Embassy of Sweden is aware on presence of many actors in education and recognizes their contributions in the sector.
2. To build a strong national and international network for CSOs to engage. TEN/MET as a secretariat has been able to recruit 200 member organizations and at the same time within the five year strategic timeframe TEN/MET will continuously assess legibility and activeness of such organizations to ensure that it works with right partners, focus, documentation and aspirations. Different from last strategic plan 2015 - 2017, the new TENMET strategy 2018 - 2022 breaks members in to zones and thematic area to allow for prioritization and capacity development initiatives.
3. To adress areas of education financing gap, inclusive education through evidence based research. As a secretatiat, TEN/MET for next five years has positioned itself to utilize research and experiences from other member organizations to appeal to the government on behalf of education sector to expand incluciveness and education budget in the sector. TEN/MET is aware of the recent inclusive strategy developed by the government with exclusion of clear articulations on how specific affected groups are going to be reached. For next five years, TENMET has indicated to capitalize on documenting gaps and sharing best practices that will promote quality and equality education in Tanzania.
4. The fourth area is enhancing effective dialogue and participation of CSOs in education partners development group and ESDC meetings. TEN/MET for next five years has innovatively designed a specific budget line to allow member organizations to meet, review, analyze and comment on proposals or government documents that are submitted to donor group for review.
The intervention’s total budget is 11.3 billion TZSH for five years, out of which the Embassy of Sweden contribution is expected to be around 5 billion and the rest 6.3b will be fundraised by TENMET from other donors. Already there are donors that have committed fund to TEN/MET but not as in longer term as Embassy of Sweden has done. CSEF- Civil Society Education Fund has confirmed support of 260,040,000 TZSH for each year of the new strategy. Porticus who has been funding TENMET last year has also committed 186,480,000 for 2018. Another committed fund for 2018 is the LANES support from government Worth of 761,113,255 and also from another donor called APHRC with 30,000,000 support. TENMET is positive that all the donors who are currently funding them will continue to do so and their expectation is high for other potential donors like NORAD, DFID, GIZ and Equality Now.

Tanzanias utbildningssektor är bred och utmaningarna är många. TEN/MET är medvetna om de utmaningar som finns i sektorn; Få klarar de nationella proven som ges i grundskolan, få elever har en god läsförståelse och ännu färre klarar av simpla matematiska uppgifter. Även på policynivå har Tanzania problem med både formulering och implementering. TEN/MET koordinerar de civilsamhällesorganisationer som är aktiva inom utbildningssektorn i Tanzania. Genom att fokusera på fyra områden ska TEN/MET bidra till en ökad kvalitet och jämställdhet inom utbildningssektorn.
1. Genom att koordinera de civilsamhällesorganisationer som finns inom utbildningssektorn kan organisationerna dela med sig av sina utmaningar och framgångar för att effektivt påverka policy på hög nivå. Ambassaden har kontakt med flertalet av civilsamhällesorganisationerna inom TEN/MET och deras bidrag till utbildningssektorn är stor.
2. Att bygga ett starkt nationellt och internationellt nätverks där civilsamhällesorganisationer kan samlas. Över 200 civilsamhällesorganisationer är medlemmar i TEN/METs och den nya strategin syftar delvis till att analysera medlemmarnas aktivitets, för att se till så att TEN/MET samarbetar med rätt organisationer, har rätt focus, dokumentation och vision. Till skillnad från föregående den strategiska planen för 2015-2017, så kommer den nya strategin för 2018 – 2022 att dela upp medlemmarna i zoner för att kunna priorietara och koordinera kapacitetsbyggnad.
3. Att påverka de finanseringsgap som finns inom utbildningssektorn genom evidensbaserad forskning. TEN/MET har de senaste åren positionerat sig för att använda forskning och erfarenheter från dess medlemmar för att påverka regeringen att utveckla en inkluderande utbildning samt att öka regeringens budget för utbildningssektorn. TEN/MET är medvetna om att regeringens nya strategi för en inkluderande utbildning exkluderar specifika grupper, så som unga mödrar. För de kommande fem åren strävar TEN/MET efter att brygga dokumentationsgap för att främja en kvalitativ och jämställd utbildning i Tanzania.
4. Att skapa en effektiv dialog och ökat deltagande av civilsamhällesorganisationer i givargruppen för utbildningsfrågor samt ESDC möten. TEN/MET har skapat en specifik budgetlinje för att tillåta att medlemmasorganisationerna kommer att mötas för att analysera och kommentara regeringens förslag och strategier för de kommande fem åren.
Budgeten för de kommande fem åren uppgår till 11.3 miljarder TZS. Ambassaden kommer att bidra med ca 5 miljarder TSH. De resterande 6.3 miljarderna kommer TEN/MET att söka från andra givare.

The long term goal of TEN/MET is to see a national education system that embraces quality education for all. TENMET is an umbrella organization with almost 200 member CSOs working in education sector in Tanzania. Since it is a member based organization, its intended outcomes are divided into two connected categories.
Secretariat. The outcome number 1 focusses on building institutional capacity of the organization and the board to be able to play effective oversight role. The new strategy 2018 - 2022 aims at recruiting new board members with education and thematic background. To blend the strategy with right skills, TENMET is also going to recruit new people over time to competitively navigate safely in a politically changing environment. TEN/MET believes that the long term goal of ensuring national education system is embracing quality education for all will not be sustainable if as an institution does not equip itself better to confornt realities on the ground.
As a Network There are four intended outcome to be achieved; To develop CSOs capacity, to strengthen the network, conduct evidence based research and lastly join hands with other CSOs to do advocacy. TEN/MET will have CSOs equipped with relevant skills, CSOs as network will get connected to regional and international affiliations and jointly with members TENMET will generate knowledge to inform policy change in education sector in Tanzania. During the time of TENMET appraisal, Tanzania' largest share of the national budget went to infrastructure and education sector is the second. According to Ministry of Finance Sector Analysis (2017/2018), The Ministry of works, communication and infrastructure has 5,541,3 billion TZSH while ministry of education has 4,706,4. Again; Interestingly, despite the increase in enrollment since 2016, education sector budget is decreasing from 16% in 2016/17 to 15% in 2017/18. One of the TEN/MET's advocacy strategy is to challenge the government to consider education as high in the agenda and increase national annual budget allocation for education sector.

The role of TENMET in general is organized in the below objectives,
1. coordinate education Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) to influence decisions in the education system in Tanzania.
ii. To strengthen TEN/MET systems and structures to carry its mandate.
iii. To generate evidence-based best practices locally, regionally, and globally to influence educational policy and practices.
iv. To advocate for gender mainstreaming in the education system to secure equitable, inclusive, and quality education for learners in Tanzania, and
v. To advocate for an education system that embraces Science, Technology, and Innovation to meet the demands of the 4th Industrial revolution. During this period, our organisation has achieved remarkable milestones, each serving as a testament to our unwavering dedication to our mission.
Below is the summary of key results attained during last year of Swedish support and across the strategy period.
- There has been an increased membership base from 184 to 232 members, an increase of 48 new members who have gone through screening and vetting by the Annual General Meeting. According to TENMET, more members, further chances to amplify the representation and advocacy.
- Contributed to the review of the Education and Training Policy 2014, version 2023 aimed at revitalising the delivery and fortifying the quality of education nationwide to withstand challenges. Integral to this effort was the incorporation of a re-entry agenda into the education system, ensuring equitable access to education for all. TENMET being the lead NGO at education sector development partners meeting which is a platform to advise the govement, is a contributing factor of influence.
- contributed to the review of curricula, ensuring graduates are equipped with the essential skills to excel in the global labour market, foster self employment, and navigate life's complexities. Emphasis was placed on integrating comprehensive life skills, technical education and sexual reproductive health education into the curriculum. TENMET view government decision to review curriculum was partly attributed by their advocacy work.
- TENMET fostered a robust partnership with the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST) that culminated in TEN/MET being granted a role to coordinate CSOs through TEN/METs National Education Caucus to develop the National Re-entry Implementation Plan. An action plan is a milestone document which TENMET will continue to follow up to ensure grils are not left behind.
- Effectively mobilised and coordinated the active involvement of TEN/MET members in a GPE multiplier grant event on 31st August 2023, resulting in a substantial collective pledge of $30,141,663.90. This financial commitment played a pivotal role in unlocking the GPE multiplier grant, underscoring the tangible impact of TEN/MET's coordination efforts in securing substantial resources for educational initiatives from domestic resource mobilisation.
- Transformed the teaching and learning environment in four schools at Mvuha District Council during the Global Action Week for Education. This involved various initiatives, such as constructing teachers' toilets at Bonye Primary School, improving flooring in a classroom at Njia Nne Primary School, procuring desks for Dutumi Primary School, and establishing a model Early Childhood Development (ECD) classroom at Mvuha Primary School.
- The Network effectively coordinated zonal meetings across all zones, fostering the exchange of expertise and facilitating mutual learning among members for improved advocacy. Last but not least, the Network organised a webinar to commemorate World Swahili Day. The event was titled "Language Matters: Enhancing Learning Outcomes with Swahili as a Medium of Instruction." During this webinar, experts debated the issues related to achieving impactful learning outcomes. The event received critical acclaim from a diverse audience from across Tanzania.
- TENMET, the Network organised a Continental Education Strategy for Africa (CESA) familiarisation meeting in Dar es Salaam, attended by 24 participants (12F, 12M) on December 11th and 12th on the SDGs and CESA. The sessions were aimed at enabling effective CSOs follow-up in the implementation of these frameworks and the alignment and coordinate alignments of strategies.
- Throughout the reporting period, TEN/MET remained committed to resource mobilisation, engaging in various meetings and initiatives to secure funding. These efforts were for example; Conducted a meeting with the European Union (EU) to update on future funding opportunities, conducted a meeting with the Swiss Embassy to explore potential funding opportunities, submitted a proposal to World Food Programme (WPF) for $200,000 over 18 months. TENMET also submitted a proposal to Education Out Loud (EOL) for $411,000 over three years. It is reported that, there is still an ongoing proposal development with the German Development Cooperation (GIZ) of about €100,000 for one year and lastly Proposal submission to Knowing-Doing Network Leadership Coalition (KDNLC) for $400,000 over two years was in the making by time report submission for year 2023 was due.
- In the pursuit of advocating for increased education financing, TEN/MET collaborated with AKUVIKIRU, AFRIWAG, and TREE OF HOPE to engage actively in the budget process at the local government level. Specifically, this collaboration was extended to Rungwa, Mkinga, and Pangani District Councils. The overarching goal was to advocate for the prioritisation of education in the LGA budgets for the forthcoming fiscal year (2024/25). As a result of their engagement, the districts plan included the improvement of teaching and learning infrastructures as key areas in local government budgets.
- During the reporting period, the Network initiated a genderresponsive budget analysis with the aim of gaining a comprehensive understanding of how national budgetary commitments align with the diverse needs of various groups in accessing quality education for the five-year period from 2019/20 to 2023/24. The study's specific objectives encompassed determining the importance of Gender Responsive Budgeting in the education sector, assessing the extent to which the education sector budget addresses gender issues, and critically examining how the findings could align with the Network's efforts to promote gender equality in access to education. The study is expected to be concluded in 2024.
- Moreover, TEN/MET crafted a spotlight report titled "How the Re-Entry Agenda in Tanzania Impacts the Achievement of SDGs 4 & 5." The report's findings were presented at the High-Level Political Forum in New York from July 10th to 19th 2023, contributing to the country's progress in attaining SDGs 4 & 5. A subsequent national dissemination meeting was held on September 19th 2023, bringing together 50 participants, including representatives from implementing organisations, local CSOs, and three ministries (PO-RALG, MoCDGWSG, MOEST), along with media coverage. The Network printed and distributed 500 copies of the brief for wider dissemination.
- The Network convened a meeting with the Permanent Parliament Budget Committee in the Dodoma Region on February 3rd 2023, aiming to enhance their understanding of gender-responsive budgeting. During the meeting, a total of nine issues were presented to the committee to address concerns related to the school learning environment and to improve learning outcomes. These issues encompassed aspects such as the availability of qualified teachers, the establishment of Early Childhood Development (ECD) centres near Alternative Education Pathways centres for teen mothers, the provision of adequate classrooms, sensitising teachers on the education-for-all agenda to eliminate stigma against teen mothers, and ensuring sufficient pit latrines in schools. The meeting involved 48 participants (19F, 29M), including representation from parliamentarians, TEN/MET Secretariat, a male gender-responsive budgeting expert, and members from various organisations. The parliamentarians pledged to incorporate a gender-responsive approach in reviewing the education budget and addressing the submitted issues to ensure inclusive education for all.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
